original_topic: evidence attribution, factuality, completeness and reliability evaluation for workplace communication systems: what exact evidence supports each decision-relevant statement, whether it is current and correctly attributed, what was omitted, and when the system should abstain
topic: evaluation of calibrated abstention, evidence completeness, and omission for free-form multi-source generation under temporal and distributional change
focus: academic gaps of the previous round

prior_gaps.description: No admitted study validates one end-to-end evaluation scheme that jointly measures claim correctness, evidence attribution correctness, citation or evidence completeness, temporal/current-state correctness, omission, calibrated uncertainty, and abstention while preserving the separate denominators of those dimensions. The corpus validates individual components or smaller combinations.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "evaluation framework" factuality attribution citation completeness temporal correctness omission uncertainty abstention language generation

prior_gaps.description: The corpus contains no direct evaluation on private workplace email or Teams-style communication with realistic revisions, quoted history, conflicting updates, delayed or out-of-order arrival, versioned attachments, and permission-constrained evidence. Target-domain fixtures and gold data therefore remain an engineering validation gap.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Build a target-domain evaluation fixture suite from synthetic, de-identified, or appropriately authorized workplace-style conversations. Include revisions, quoted-message history, contradictory and superseding updates, delayed and out-of-order events, attachment versions, and permission boundaries. Define gold claim-to-evidence links, temporal truth state, allowed evidence visibility, omissions, and expected abstentions, then run the system against these fixtures as regression and acceptance benchmarks.

prior_gaps.description: Calibration and selective prediction for unconstrained free-form generation remain insufficiently answered by this corpus. The calibration study explicitly excludes free-form abstractive QA, while the evidence-sufficiency benchmark measures behavioral abstention in controlled QA conditions rather than calibrated probabilities for open-ended outputs.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "selective prediction" "free-form generation" calibration abstention risk coverage language models

prior_gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a general method for measuring evidence completeness when a generated claim is compound, partially supported, supported by multiple sources, or requires temporally versioned evidence. Existing citation-recall methods and attributed-QA criteria cover narrower settings.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "citation completeness" compound claims partial support multi-source temporal evidence attribution evaluation

prior_gaps.description: Report-level omission and coverage of decision-relevant content remain underexplored in this corpus. Pyramid evaluates reference-summary content units and ALCE evaluates citation support coverage, but neither establishes omission detection for evolving workplace work items or due information.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "summary completeness" omission detection decision-focused evaluation content coverage evolving information

prior_gaps.description: A target-domain human-review protocol still has to specify representative or risk-stratified sampling, minimum human-review volume, multi-rater adjudication, confusion matrices, abstention handling, coverage reporting, and validation of any LLM-assisted judge against independent human judgments.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Specify and version a review protocol using established annotation and validation practices: define representative and risk-stratified sampling strata, minimum review counts or confidence targets, blinded independent ratings, adjudication rules, label definitions, confusion matrices, abstention and unanswerable categories, coverage metrics, and inter-rater agreement. Validate any LLM judge on a held-out human-labeled set and report judge-human agreement and error slices before using it for acceptance.

prior_gaps.description: The corpus demonstrates evaluator gaming and directional judge bias but does not provide a project-specific procedure for preventing optimization against the same automatic evaluator used for acceptance. Independent holdouts, evaluator separation, and regression checks remain an engineering validation problem.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Separate development and acceptance evaluators, maintain hidden or access-controlled holdout fixtures, prohibit tuning directly against final acceptance outputs, rotate or diversify evaluator prompts/models where appropriate, periodically re-score samples with independent humans, and add regression tests for known judge-bias and reward-hacking failure modes. Track evaluator-version changes so gains caused only by evaluator drift can be detected.

prior_gaps.description: Calibration under continuing temporal or distributional change remains open in this corpus. Cross-domain calibration transfer is imperfect and benchmark aging can change the correct target over time, but no admitted paper establishes a calibrated selective-prediction method for a non-stationary communication stream.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "uncertainty calibration" non-stationary streams temporal distribution shift selective prediction language models
